name: inflow-predicts-funnel-endpoint-v1
status: FROZEN before computing any inflow value. Zero forward passes -- every model-side quantity comes from results/argmax_census_hardened.json, already stored and stamped.
epistemic_tier: TIER 1 for H1/H2 and TIER 2 for H3, and labelled so. H1 and H2 test a prediction made by an OUTSIDE paper (Fu et al. 2021) that was read on 20 Aug 2026 in F170; no inflow number has been computed by anyone here, so nothing about the outcome is known. H3 is TIER 2 because the class split (8 funnel / 6 none / 2 fragmented / 1 borderline) has been known since F90 and informs the prediction.
motivation: F170 read Fu, Lam, So & Shi (arXiv:2012.14660, AAAI 2021) in full. Their Corollary 1.2 splits an upper bound on repetition probability into named 'outflow' and 'inflow' terms, where 'the inflow for a word is the probability sum of all words that take it as the subsequent word', and they conclude that 'high inflow words are more likely to go back to itself and cause the repetition problem'. Their thesis is that this is a property of LANGUAGE: 'the repetition problem is caused by the language itself.' They never measure a model's own conditional -- every transition matrix in their paper is corpus word counts. This project has the complementary half: a census of 17 models' argmax maps with stored endpoint tokens. So their theory makes a checkable prediction about our data, and our data makes a checkable objection to their thesis. This runs both directions.

hypotheses.H1_endpoint_is_high_inflow: the token a model's map funnels to is a HIGH-INFLOW token under corpus bigram statistics computed with that model's own tokenizer -- i.e. Fu et al.'s mechanism, measured on the object they never measured
hypotheses.H2_inflow_beats_frequency: endpoint tokens rank higher on INFLOW than on raw FREQUENCY, against a frequency-matched control. THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING TEST. Fu et al. draw exactly this distinction themselves -- 'it is not the high-frequency words, but the high inflow words that really lead to repetition' -- so H1 without H2 supports only the trivial claim that models get stuck on common tokens, which nobody disputes and which needs no theory.
hypotheses.H3_language_thesis_fails_across_models: if the geometry were caused by 'the language itself', models reading the same corpus should agree. They do not: 8 of 17 are funnels and 9 are not. H3 predicts that inflow CONCENTRATION (computed per model on the same corpus) does NOT separate funnel from non-funnel models, which would locate the difference in the weights rather than in the language.

frozen.corpus: wikitext-103-raw-v1, train split, already cached locally. Chosen because it is the corpus Fu et al. themselves used for their ARP experiment, not because of anything known about our models.
frozen.corpus_size: the first 20,000,000 characters of non-empty lines, joined by newline. Frozen here. A newline-joined corpus is deliberate: the newline is a modal endpoint for 7 of 17 models and excluding it would rig the test.
frozen.tokenization: each model's OWN tokenizer, loaded from the local cache, applied to the same character stream. No special tokens added.
frozen.inflow_estimator: C[a,b] = count of adjacent token pairs. B[a,b] = C[a,b] / sum_b C[a,b] (row-normalised, matching Fu et al.'s Algorithm 1, which divides by the row sum). inflow(t) = sum_a B[a,t]. This is Corollary 1.2's inflow term verbatim: the probability sum over all predecessors that take t as the subsequent token.
frozen.frequency_estimator: unigram token count on the same stream
frozen.endpoint_token: modal_endpoint_token from results/argmax_census_hardened.json, per model, per census seed. A model enters only if BOTH seeds agree on the modal token; models whose two seeds disagree are reported and excluded, because the quantity being predicted must itself be stable.
frozen.class: the stored cls field: funnel / none / fragmented / borderline. Frozen as recorded in F90; not recomputed here.

the_control_that_makes_this_non_vacuous: FREQUENCY-MATCHED NULL. For each model's endpoint token e, take the 50 tokens whose unigram count is nearest to e's in log-frequency (excluding e), and compute e's inflow percentile WITHIN that matched set. If endpoint tokens are merely frequent, this percentile is ~50 by construction and H1's raw success is exposed as a frequency artefact. H2 is judged on this percentile and on nothing else. Frozen before any number is computed.

kill_conditions.K1_H1_dead: if the endpoint token's inflow percentile (over the whole vocabulary) is below 90 for a majority of readable models, Fu et al.'s mechanism does not describe this map's endpoints and H1 is dead
kill_conditions.K2_vacuity_of_H1: if the SINGLE most-inflow token of a model's corpus equals its endpoint token for most models, H1 is true by a trivial rule and the trivial rule's own success rate is reported AS the chance baseline. H1 must beat that rule, not merely agree with it.
kill_conditions.K3_H2_decides: if the frequency-matched percentile is not above 50 for a majority of readable models, then inflow adds nothing to frequency, and the correct statement is that the map funnels to COMMON tokens rather than to HIGH-INFLOW ones. That would leave Fu et al.'s specific claim unsupported on this data while leaving the trivial claim intact, and it must be reported in exactly those words.
kill_conditions.K4_coverage: a model is NOT DECIDABLE if its endpoint token does not occur in the corpus at all, or occurs fewer than 100 times. This is expected for models whose endpoint is not English -- polyglot-ko, bloom and LFM2 have endpoints in Korean, Spanish and Korean respectively -- and their exclusion is a statement about the CORPUS being wrong for them, never about the theory being wrong. English wikitext cannot test a Korean model's endpoint and no result will pretend otherwise.
kill_conditions.K5_balance: H3 requires at least 2 funnel and 2 non-funnel models to survive K4. Checked with gatecheck.balance, whose chance level is the majority-class rate, never 50%.
kill_conditions.K6_H3_is_a_null: H3 predicts NO separation. A null result is only informative if the comparison had the power to show one, so the observed separation is reported WITH the spread of each group, and if the groups overlap the verdict is stated as 'does not separate' and never as 'proves language-independence'.

refusals_recorded_before_numbers: no p-value on 17 models; the cluster count is the model count
no causal claim. Corpus bigram inflow is not the model's conditional, and a correspondence between them is an observation about training data, not a mechanism inside the network.

no claim that this VALIDATES Fu et al. Their theorem is about an upper bound on repetition probability in a Markov generation model. Agreement of our endpoints with their inflow term is consistent with their account and is not a test of their bound.
rank correlation between inflow rank and phi is permitted ONLY if at least 10 models survive K4, which is this project's ten-cluster floor from F149. Below that it is not computed.
what_would_make_me_wrong: the cleanest refutation of H2 is that endpoint tokens turn out to be the most FREQUENT tokens and nothing more. That is a real possibility -- '\n', '0', '1', ',' are among the commonest tokens in any corpus -- and it is why the frequency-matched control is frozen before the run rather than added after seeing that H1 passed.
owed: nothing new. F169's outstanding items (four SNIPPET-grade papers unread, gate not re-run at protocol depth) are unaffected by this run and remain owed.
amendment_log: 20 Aug 2026, BEFORE the run and BEFORE any inflow value was computed: H3 referred to 'inflow CONCENTRATION' without pinning a formula, which would have let the outcome choose it. Pinned now: concentration := max_t inflow(t), the single largest inflow term. Chosen because it is the quantity that magnifies Fu et al.'s Corollary 1.2 bound -- their argument is that ONE token with large inflow is enough. The top-10 inflow mass share is also reported as a shape descriptor and is NOT a criterion.

20 Aug 2026, BEFORE the run: the frozen text says H1's percentile is taken 'over the whole vocabulary'. Tokens that never occur in the corpus have inflow exactly 0, so including them inflates every percentile. The registered whole-vocabulary percentile REMAINS THE PRIMARY and is reported as such; a stricter percentile over tokens with corpus count > 0 is reported ALONGSIDE it, explicitly labelled as not the registered quantity. Recording this rather than silently switching to the stricter one, which would be choosing a criterion after seeing its shape.
